Augustus.text: Talkative, easygoing co-owner of the Hat Creek outfit and Call's old Ranger partner, now helping drive the herd toward Montana. He rescued Lorena from Blue Duck's camp, helped hang Jake Spoon's gang, then left Lorena at the Platte ranch of Clara, the woman he once loved. At the Powder River in Wyoming he has just helped bury Deets, tying his old Ranger medal to the grave.

Pea Eye.text: Slow, loyal hand and former Ranger, half deaf in one ear from an old Indian battle, who has followed Call for years. He has stuck with the herd from Lonesome Dove through river crossings, Ogallala's revels and the brutal waterless stretch into Wyoming. He is now camped with the crew beside Deets's fresh grave where Salt Creek meets the Powder River.

Call.text: Stern, driven co-owner of the Hat Creek outfit, determined to be first to graze cattle in Montana. He has pushed the herd across the plains, hanged his old comrade Jake with the Suggs gang, nearly beaten an Army scout to death in Ogallala and bought horses from Clara. After losing Deets to a starving band's lance, he carved the scout's grave board on the Powder River in Wyoming.

Newt.text: The youngest hand of the Hat Creek outfit, a boy raised in Lonesome Dove whose mother is dead, eager to prove himself to Call. He has weathered stampedes, lost his horse Mouse, tasted Ogallala and been given a sorrel by Clara, who offered him work. He is now with the herd in Wyoming, camped by the grave of Deets, his longtime friend.

Lorena.text: A former Lonesome Dove prostitute who left town with Jake Spoon, was kidnapped and abused by Blue Duck, and was rescued by Augustus. She traveled north with him alongside the herd, slowly recovering and dreading meeting Clara. By the end of chapter 88 she has accepted Clara's invitation to stay at her Platte River horse ranch while Augustus and the herd move on.

Lippy.text: A Lonesome Dove saloon piano player in a battered bowler, raised in St. Louis, who signed on with the drive and has been kept with the horses and wagon. He led the young hands on a spree in Ogallala and plans to master a new accordion before Montana. At Deets's grave on the Powder River he weeps and wishes he had never left home.

Dish Boggett.text: Top hand of the Hat Creek outfit, hopelessly devoted to Lorena since Lonesome Dove. He guarded her tent while left in charge of the herd in Kansas, got clubbed by an Army scout in Ogallala, and resents Augustus for leaving Lorena behind at Clara's. He is now with the herd on the Powder River in Wyoming, camped by Deets's grave.

Deets.text: The outfit's trusted scout, who served Call and Augustus for some thirty years, finding safe river crossings and tracking thieves along the trail. Homesick for the Rio Grande and uneasy about the north, he guided the herd through the brutal dry stretch. In chapter 90 he was fatally lanced by a young brave while lifting a blind child, and lies buried by the Powder River.

July Johnson.text: The sheriff of Fort Smith who rode out after Jake Spoon and lost his deputy Roscoe, the boy Joe and Janey to a killer on the Canadian. Chasing his runaway wife Elmira, he survived a lame horse and snakebite only to be rebuffed by her in Ogallala. He has now chosen to stay at Clara's Platte River ranch, working horses and caring for his infant son Martin.

Allen O'Brien.text: A homesick Irishman found with his brother Sean, lost and hungry, in Mexico and taken on by the outfit; Sean later died in a nest of water moccasins at the Nueces. Allen still mourns Ireland and the young wife he left there. After a night drinking in Ogallala he rejoined the herd and is now camped with it by Deets's grave on the Powder River.

Jasper Fant.text: A cowboy from upriver of Lonesome Dove who joined the drive, nervous of every river crossing and sure he will drown. He danced a jig after the herd swam the Republican safely and caroused with the others in Ogallala. Wishing he had stayed in Texas, he is now with the herd on the Powder River in Wyoming, camped by Deets's grave.

Pete Spettle.text: One of two barefoot sons of a poor widow whom Call hired on, walking to Lonesome Dove with his brother Bill, who was later killed by lightning in Indian Territory. Pete went along on the young hands' spree in Ogallala. His horse bolted on the way back to camp, and as of these chapters his whereabouts are unknown.

Jimmy Rainey.text: One of two Rainey brothers whose family promised them to Call for the drive north. He has ridden with the herd through Kansas and Nebraska and joined the boys' night out in Ogallala, where Augustus tipped them and Lippy got them drunk. He made it through the dry drive into Wyoming and is now camped with the outfit by Deets's grave on the Powder River.

Ben Rainey.text: The other Rainey brother hired by Call at his family's ranch, a young hand who once feared drowning in the Red River. He has followed the herd north through Kansas and Nebraska and went carousing in Ogallala with Newt and the other boys. He is now with the outfit in Wyoming, camped beside Deets's grave where Salt Creek joins the Powder River.

Needle Nelson.text: A Hat Creek hand from north of San Antonio, a fretful sort who worries about reaching the far northern rivers before winter. He spent a night carousing in Ogallala before straggling back to camp hungover. He has come through the waterless stretch into Wyoming and is now camped with the herd by Deets's grave on the Powder River.

Bert Borum.text: A cheerful hand from Brownsville who joined the outfit during the branding near Lonesome Dove. He has ridden the whole way north, wondering whether the treeless plains run clear to Canada, and spent a night carousing in Ogallala. He is now with the herd on the Powder River in Wyoming, camped beside Deets's grave.

Soupy Jones.text: A hand who joined the outfit at the herd camp near Lonesome Dove, having just come from Bastrop, where his wife died. He has ridden north with the herd and caroused in Ogallala, coming back hungover and unimpressed with Nebraska. He is now with the outfit in Wyoming, camped by Deets's grave where Salt Creek joins the Powder River.

Elmira.text: July Johnson's wife, a former Kansas prostitute who secretly fled Fort Smith while pregnant to find her old lover Dee Boot. She traveled with hide hunters to Clara's ranch, gave birth there and abandoned the baby, then found Dee jailed and later hanged in Ogallala. Rebuffing July, she has set out east by wagon with Big Zwey, toward Sioux country and St. Louis.

Big Zwey.text: A huge buffalo hunter who was drawn to Elmira on the whiskey boat, killed a trader over her and brought her north to Ogallala. He protected her from Luke, carried her to a doctor when she collapsed, and was troubled when she left her newborn behind. He is now driving her east from Ogallala by wagon, worried about warnings of Sioux.

Po Campo.text: The outfit's odd, resourceful cook, who walked into camp with his donkey and won the crew over with unusual dishes. Blue Duck killed his three sons years ago on the Llano Estacado. Having warned of the dry stretch beyond the Platte, he lingered sadly at its water before the herd turned northwest, and he is now with the outfit by Deets's grave on the Powder River.

Luke.text: A rough hide hunter who traveled north with Elmira and Big Zwey, harassing her until Zwey smashed his head against a wagon wheel. He came with them to Clara's ranch and on to Ogallala. He has since left the party and hired on with traders bound for Santa Fe.

Sally.text: One of the girls of Clara's household at her horse ranch on the North Platte, near Ogallala. She has watched July Johnson arrive and settle in to help with the horses and his baby, Martin, and joined the picnic and wading when Augustus's party visited. She remains at the ranch, where Lorena has now come to stay.

Clara.text: A blunt, capable Nebraska horse rancher, once courted by Augustus in Austin before she married horse trader Bob Allen, who now lies helpless after an injury. She took in Elmira's abandoned baby and persuaded July to stay and raise him. She welcomed Augustus, sold Call horses at a hard price, and has invited Lorena to stay with her at the ranch on the Platte.

Cholo.text: Clara's loyal ranch hand at her horse ranch on the North Platte, who helps her geld colts and runs errands to Ogallala. He met the exhausted July on the river road and brought him to the ranch. In chapter 88 he rides off with Augustus toward Ogallala to fetch the clothes bought for Lorena.

Bob Allen.text: Clara's husband, a Kentucky horse trader who brought her to the hard Nebraska plains and once sold horses to the Army. He now lies paralyzed and unconscious at their ranch on the North Platte. Clara and July tend him while the household goes on around him.

Betsey.text: One of the girls of Clara's household at her horse ranch on the North Platte. She has seen July Johnson come to stay and care for his infant son, and waded in the river with Newt during the picnic when Augustus's party visited. She remains at the ranch, where Lorena has now been invited to stay.
